dedupe_keys.name: measuring broadband australia dataset releases accc

description: The Measuring Broadband Australia programme of the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission measures the performance of fixed broadband services using volunteer households that receive a Whitebox, a small device that runs thousands of automated tests on their connection. The ACCC uses the measurements to report average speeds and other metrics for groups of volunteers, such as those on National Broadband Network fixed-line and fixed-wireless services, and with each report it releases a de-identified summary dataset on data.gov.au. The Report 31 release of December 2025 contains test results for all Whiteboxes used in that report, covering download and upload speeds, latency and outages, as CSV files with a guide to the data in PDF; earlier reports have their own dataset releases on the portal. Coverage: Australia, periodic reports (Report 31 in December 2025). Format and access: CSV and PDF guide per report from data.gov.au, free under CC BY 2.5 Australia. Caveats: volunteers are a panel, not a random sample of all users; results are summarised per Whitebox to protect privacy; methods change between reports. Simulation uses: service performance and outage frequency of fixed broadband, calibration of network performance models, and comparison of technologies such as fibre, fixed wireless and satellite. Related records: the NBN footprint dataset gives where each technology is used, and RTR-NetTest and Ookla open data provide crowdsourced counterparts.
